copy.title: The Buffett Money File
copy.desc: An interactive, fully sourced map of Warren Buffett’s family: Berkshire Hathaway, the foundations his children run, the stock you can buy, and the money on the public record.
copy.eyebrow: File #013 · The Buffett family · Data as of
copy.h1: He’s giving away 99%. His kids decide where it goes. We followed the money.
copy.lede: Who’s who, the foundation each child runs, the Berkshire shares you can buy, and the money on the public record. Every number links to its source.
copy.familyLede: Tap anyone to open their file. Warren’s three children are adults who each run a foundation he funds, and one of them now chairs Berkshire.
copy.investLede: Berkshire Hathaway trades on the New York Stock Exchange as BRK.A and BRK.B. The family foundations get Berkshire shares from Warren every year, but they aren’t companies you can invest in.
copy.moneyLede: Nearly all of it is Berkshire Class A stock, which he converts to Class B shares and gives away every year. Only Warren has a published net worth.
copy.recordLede: What Berkshire’s own news releases, SEC filings and its proxy statement show. Filings and reporting, not guesses.
copy.trailLede: From three shares of Cities Service at 11 to a $144 billion fortune he’s giving away.
copy.calcYearsK: Years to earn what Warren has
copy.ledgerFoot: * Class A shares carry far more votes than Class B shares, which is why his share of the votes is bigger than his share of the company. “Our sum” means simple addition of the linked filings or reports.

summary.t: Married Warren in 1952 and stayed married to him until she died in 2004, though they lived apart from 1977. She sang professionally and served on Berkshire’s board.

record.t: She owned 2.2% of Berkshire, worth about $3 billion, when she died. Nearly all of it went to the foundation that now bears her name.

summary.t: Took control of Berkshire Hathaway, then a textile maker, in 1965 and ran it for six decades. Greg Abel became CEO on Jan. 1, 2026. In September 2026 his son Howard succeeded him as chair, and Warren became chairman emeritus.

owns.t: Chairman emeritus and a director. After his July 2026 gift he owned 188,290 Class A shares, about 38.2% of that class, an SEC filing shows.

record.t: He has promised more than 99% of his wealth to charity and has given away more than $72 billion so far, mostly through the Gates Foundation and his children’s foundations, Forbes says.
He told The Wall Street Journal in 2024 that more than 99% of what remains will go to a charitable trust overseen by his three children. The Gates Foundation gets nothing from his estate.

On July 14, 2026, he converted 8,000 Class A shares into 12 million Class B shares. He gave 9 million to the Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation and 1 million to each of his children’s foundations, about $6 billion in all. For the first time in 20 years, none went to the Gates Foundation; The Wall Street Journal reported he was waiting for a review of the foundation’s past ties to Jeffrey Epstein.
“My goal is to dispose of all of my Berkshire shares within about eight years,” he wrote in July 2026. Whatever is left goes to the four family foundations by Dec. 31, 2034.
As of March 2026 he held 30.2% of Berkshire’s voting power but a 13.7% economic interest, the 2026 proxy statement shows.

facts.t: He bought his first stock at 11: three shares of Cities Service Preferred for himself and three for his sister.
He still lives in the Omaha house he bought for $31,500 in 1958, and called it the third-best investment he ever made.
He bought a beach house in Laguna Beach, Calif., in the 1970s for $150,000 and sold it in 2018 for about $7.5 million.

summary.t: She lived with Warren after his first wife, Susan, moved to San Francisco in 1977, and the three stayed close. They married on his 76th birthday in 2006.
Chairs the Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation and the Sherwood Foundation, both in Omaha, and has been a Berkshire director since 2021.

record.t: The Sherwood Foundation received 1 million Berkshire Class B shares, worth about $496 million, in July 2026.

facts.t: She started the Sherwood Foundation in 1999 and the Buffett Early Childhood Fund in 2005.

summary.t: A Berkshire director since 1993 who became chairman in September 2026. He has run the Howard G. Buffett Foundation since 1999 and farms in Illinois.

record.t: “Greg runs the company; Howard will guard its culture and values,” Warren said when Howard became chairman.

facts.t: His foundation had given more than $800 million in humanitarian aid to Ukraine by August 2025.
He served as sheriff of Macon County, Illinois, in 2017 and 2018, and has been a Coca-Cola director since 2010.

summary.t: Emmy-winning composer who co-chairs the NoVo Foundation with his wife, Jennifer. It works to empower girls and women and reduce violence against them.

facts.t: He scored the “Fire Dance” scene in Dances with Wolves.
At 19 he got about $90,000 of Berkshire stock and spent it on his music career. CNBC wrote in 2020 that it would have been worth about $300 million.

summary.t: Omaha stockbroker and Republican congressman from Nebraska, 1943–1949 and 1951–1953.
Born Leila Stahl. She married Howard Buffett in 1925.
